paper.title: Instance-Optimal Acyclic Join Processing Without Regret: Engineering the Yannakakis Algorithm in Column Stores

risks: The inspect-only probe did not execute the build or benchmark, so dependency stability, end-to-end runtime, and reproducibility are not yet established.
A GPU requirement was detected and may raise hardware cost or reduce reproducibility unless a CPU-only evaluation path is confirmed.
The repository appears to include a sizable DuckDB-derived codebase, which may make builds, instrumentation, and sandboxing heavier than a focused benchmark module.
Full reproduction across 1,849 queries may exceed a practical evaluation budget and should be reduced to bounded sampled workloads.
The paper is too recent to show citation or external adoption, and the repository currently has no reported stars.

contribution.title: Cardinality-aware join-tree rewriting for Yannakakis plans
contribution.summary: Rewrite a cardinality-annotated binary join tree into an equivalent, cost-aware shape before lowering it to a two-phase NSA/Yannakakis semijoin plan. The chosen rooting, orientation, and reassociation affect semijoin scheduling, final join order, and intermediate-result costs.
contribution.paper_location: Section 4, in the plan-generation and cost-based rewriting discussion for two-phase NSA/Yannakakis execution.
contribution.metric: End-to-end query latency and regret or speedup relative to the original binary plan, measured with binaryjoin_vs_yannakakis and its timings CSV. Require equal query outputs for correctness. A fixed, small Stats-CEB subset can be evaluated in minutes on the reproduced CPU-only environment.
